title: B2 First – wyrażenia
description: Wyrażenia typowe dla zadań egzaminu B2 First (Reading and Use of English, Part 1–3): kolokacje, wyrażenia przyimkowe, czasowniki frazowe i rodziny wyrazów. Oryginalne zdania, nie z arkuszy.

cards.text: The new law will {{come into}} effect next month.
cards.note: come into effect; też: take effect.

cards.text: The company is {{on the verge of}} bankruptcy.
cards.note: on the verge of + rzeczownik lub -ing.

cards.text: The driver had a {{narrow|lucky}} escape when the car hit the wall.
cards.note: a narrow escape – cudem uniknąć niebezpieczeństwa.

cards.text: We should {{take into account|take into consideration}} the high cost of living.
I {{couldn't help|could not help}} laughing when he fell off his chair.
She {{is bound to|is sure to|is certain to}} pass the exam. She has worked so hard.
He {{was supposed to|was meant to|was due to}} call me an hour ago.
cards.note: be supposed to – oczekiwanie lub plan, który się nie spełnił.

cards.text: The film {{lived up to}} my expectations.
It's {{no use|no good}} complaining. Nobody will listen.
By {{the time}} we arrived, the film had already started.
{{Regardless of|Irrespective of}} the weather, the match will take place.
The mayor {{is expected to|is due to|is set to}} announce the new plans tomorrow.
We had {{no choice but to|no alternative but to}} wait for the next train.
cards.note: have no choice but to + bezokolicznik.

cards.text: It {{never occurred to|didn't occur to}} me that she might be lying.
cards.note: It never occurred to me + that.

cards.text: The company {{is in the process of|is in the middle of}} moving to a bigger office.
She {{takes pride in}} her work and never leaves it unfinished.
cards.note: take pride in + rzeczownik lub -ing; też: be proud of.

cards.text: Most of the residents {{are in favour of|are in favor of}} the new bridge.
cards.note: in favour of – BrE; in favor of – AmE.

cards.text: I {{am under the impression|have the impression|get the impression}} that he doesn't really like the job.
I {{came across|stumbled across|ran across}} an old photo while I was tidying my room.
Don't {{put off}} doing your homework until the last minute.
They {{turned up|showed up}} an hour late, so we missed the beginning.
The meeting {{dragged on|went on}} for hours and nobody wanted to speak.
Her {{kindness}} surprised everyone at the party.
It was a very {{enjoyable}} evening.
He is a very {{creative}} designer.
Climbing without a rope is {{dangerous}}.
The ending of the book was {{disappointing}}.
She spoke {{confidently}} in front of the whole school.
There is a lot of {{unemployment}} in this region.
Many young people have {{unrealistic}} expectations about work.

cards.note: Pułapka: eventually = w końcu, nie „ewentualnie” (to: possibly, if necessary).
warn someone about/of something; warn someone not to do something.
admit + -ing: He admitted breaking the window.
adapt to + rzeczownik; też: adjust to.
a range of – wiele rodzajów (a range of colours).
